title: Ashbourne retail edge pilot jot
body:
Context / quick summary:
- Ashbourne Retail: 12 pilot kiosks across 3 flagship stores. Goal: realtime conversational product search + receipt-parsing at point-of-sale (no cloud roundtrip ideally).
- Pilot mode: private deployment (VPC), single rack per store (edge appliance), model pinned to a smaller, quantized LLM variant. Need <150ms median token latency for short prompts (recommendations/FAQ).

Call notes (2025-01-12 kickoff):
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood), Samir (Redwood SE), Leo (Ashbourne infra lead), Priya (Ashbourne product), Hannah (store ops).
- Business ask: reduce returns friction and speed up in-store assistance. Primary UX is typed or voice-short prompts at kiosk.
- Non-functional: strict PII rules (no customer phone/email leaving VPC), 3s max end-to-end for a full multi-turn session.
- Ops: stores have 1x edge appliance (server) with 2x A10G GPUs on premise behind NAT. Bandwidth intermittent; prefer local inference.

Technical capture (requirements + constraints):
- Model selection: want open-ish model to avoid licensing costs. We proposed Redwood-compact-v2-8q (8-bit quant, recommended) or a distilled 3B as fallback.
- Memory: A10G + 24GB GPU RAM. With KV cache and 8k context, 8q model likely fits but need runtime mem plan. Prioritize lower kv-cache retention to keep mem headroom.
- Tokenization: receipts and product SKUs require consistent tokenizer; add pre-token normalization step (remove store-specific SKU prefixes via rule).
- Caching: enable prefix caching for static prompts (store inventory corpus + policy snippets). We'll test cache hit rates; recommend TTL 48h for inventory snapshots.
- Privacy/KMS: Ashbourne uses vendor-managed KMS; they asked if Redwood can integrate customer KMS inside VPC control plane. Follow-up with security team.
- Routing/fallback: if GPU saturated or network partitions, fallback to hosted API (but Must not send PII). Need automatic scrub before fallback and clear audit logs when fallback used.

Gotchas & unknowns (red flags to resolve):
- GPU swap/perf: A10G isn't as predictable under bursty traffic (multiple kiosks hitting simultaneously). Need a throttling policy per-store to preserve SLO for all kiosks.
- Cold start: first request after idle has ~500ms extra setup (disk -> GPU). Consider pre-warm cron or a heartbeat ping from kiosk manager.
- Audio path: kiosks will send short audio clips; transcription options: do local whisper-small on CPU or send to hosted ASR? Local CPU transcribe will increase latency and CPU usage; we should test whisper-small on the edge appliance before deciding.
- Inventory freshness: they want near-real-time inventory (minutes). Can't re-download full snapshot frequently; propose delta sync + inventory index pushed to cache. Need data schema from Ashbourne.
- PCI/Network: network egress allowed only to specific Redwood IPs in dedicated breakout; confirm with their network team. Also firewall rules for control plane -> edge appliance (for rollouts) need to be ironed out.

Short experiments to run (MVP):
1) On-prem inference footprint test (Samir): deploy quantized model on A10G emulator, run 1/2/4 kiosk concurrency to measure median token latency, peak GPU mem, and KV cache impact. Collect perf traces.
2) Pre-tokenization rules (Maya + Priya): build small rule engine to normalize SKUs and masked PII patterns; create 200 synthetic receipts to test tokenization token counts.
3) ASR microbenchmark (Leo): run whisper-small on CPU vs hosted ASR for 2s audio median; measure total time and CPU contention.
4) Fallback scrub demo (Maya): create a demo flow where PII fields are detected and redacted before fallback to hosted API; include audit log entry.

Immediate action items (who/when):
- Samir: run model footprint tests and upload CSV perf results to linked PR (due 2025-01-19).
- Leo: confirm firewall & egress constraints and share network diagram (due 2025-01-16).
- Priya: provide inventory schema and example snapshots (due 2025-01-15).
- Maya: prototype pre-tokenization + redaction script and push to github, include sample receipts (due 2025-01-18).
- Security sync: set 30min meeting to discuss KMS integration + audit requirements (Maya to schedule with Ashbourne security + Redwood security) (target 2025-01-14).

Notes-to-self / quick reminders:
- Keep fallback 🔒: fallback must never transmit raw customer PII. If cannot redact confidently, route to 'error' state and return safe fallback message.
- Consider quantization fallback policy: if model generation quality drops below threshold on small prompts (we'll check BLEU/EM-like heuristics on retrieval), automatically route critical flows to a slightly larger model.
- Pre-warm strategy: use a lightweight ping every 30s for active store hours (store hours 9am-9pm local). Might add cost but reduces tail latency.

Potential follow-ups for pilot next week:
- Demo checklist: 1) simple kiosk convo (search -> product card), 2) receipt parse -> autofill return form, 3) offline degraded flow (no network) -> show fallback to cached results.
- Success metrics: median token latency <150ms, end-to-end <1.5s for typical query, accuracy of receipt extraction >95 on our sample set, no PII leaks in fallback tests.

Raw snippets / quick commands (for Samir):
- Start local perf run: python infra/bench/run_inference.py --model redwood-compact-v2-8q --gpus 2 --concurrency 4 --prompt-file tests/ashbourne/prompts-short.json --trace out/ashbourne-run.csv
- Token-normalizer quick regex (POSIX): s/STORE_[A-Z]{3}-(\d{6})/\1/g  # strip store prefix from SKUs

Open questions to chase in security meeting:
- Can we get KMS HSM-backed key provisioning in their VPC? Or will they allow Redwood-managed CMKs scoped to that account?
- Audit log retention requirement (Ashbourne asked for 12 months vs Redwood default 90d). If 12 months we need storage + RBAC plan.

End of jot. Will tidy into formal pilot-runbook once the perf numbers come in. For now this is working scratchpad: lots of TODOs, ephemeral notes, and a capture of the kickoff call.

-- Maya
